facts.statement: The study presents a new computational method called optimized multiple temporal interference stimulation (omTIS) designed to control brain activity in multiple areas at once.
facts.subject: computational

facts.statement: The method uses multiple electrodes and computer simulations to create focused electrical fields that can be aimed at different brain regions without interfering with each other.
facts.subject: computational

facts.statement: The new technique was tested in computer models, gel-like materials that mimic brain tissue, and live mice.
facts.subject: animals

facts.statement: In these tests, the new method was better than the standard version of temporal interference stimulation at targeting specific spots and moving the target around.
facts.subject: animals

facts.statement: The authors conclude that this approach offers a way to precisely control widely spread brain circuits without surgery.
facts.subject: computational
